text:
Connor Brown has given New Jersey seven points in 12 games, four goals among them, and the goals are the part to treat carefully. He has scored on 26.7% of his shots, nearly double what our numbers expect, and his finishing is 1.8 goals ahead of his chances. One of the four was an empty-netter in Toronto.

The five-on-five numbers are the real concern. The Devils take only 44% of the shot attempts with him on the ice, more than ten points worse than when he sits, which is a lot for a depth winger on a team that has been winning. His shot ranks in the 9th percentile for speed by NHL Edge, so the scoring comes from where he goes, not how hard he shoots.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking gives him one signature from last season: 19% of his setups went across the royal road (the pass that pulls a goalie side to side), against 7% for a typical forward. That passing is why he's useful. The shooting percentage is what comes back down.
headline: Brown is finishing well above his usual
